shortDescription: Craft Quark's biome-targeted Pathfinder's Quills instead of only trading for them.
oneLiner: Lets you craft Quark's Pathfinder's Quill yourself - one feather, one eye of ender and one block that matches the biome you want to find (sand for desert, podzol for old growth pine taiga, cherry leaves for cherry grove) - instead of having to trade a cartographer or wandering trader for it.

requiredMods.evidence: src/main/java/net/geraldhofbauer/vanillaplusadditions/modules/pathfinder_quills/PathfinderQuillsModule.java:55-58 - shouldInitialize() returns ModList.get().isLoaded("quark"); without it AbstractModule.initialize (core/AbstractModule.java:90-105) logs "Module '{}' is disabled and will not be initialized" and returns at :96-99, so onInitialize() never runs and neither the serializer nor the reload listener is registered. The recipe calls org.violetmoon.quark.content.tools.item.PathfindersQuillItem.forBiome(...) at modules/pathfinder_quills/recipe/PathfinderQuillRecipe.java:76 and :87 (import at :14). Compile-classpath side: build.gradle:152-160 (compileOnly Quark + Zeta, no localRuntime). Quark is NOT declared in src/main/resources/META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml - runtime gate only.
requiredMods.whatItAdds: Everything the module acts on. Quark owns the item quark:pathfinders_quill and the public factory PathfindersQuillItem.forBiome(String biomeId, int color) that stamps the TARGET_BIOME/BIOME_COLOR data components; Quark also owns the quill's actual biome-search behaviour. Without Quark the module is fully inert - no registry entry, no recipes, nothing to craft.

events: net.neoforged.neoforge.event.AddReloadListenerEvent (NeoForge.EVENT_BUS, instance registered in onInitialize at PathfinderQuillsModule.java:63; handler PathfinderQuillsModule.onAddReloadListener at :71-77, returns immediately unless isModuleEnabled()) - the module's only event subscription. It attaches an inner PreparableReloadListener named "vanillaplusadditions_pathfinder_quill_recipes" (:96-115) that waits on the preparation barrier and then runs applyQuillRecipes on the game executor. Registration of the recipe serializer is not an event handler but a DeferredRegister on the mod event bus (:41-45 for the entry, :62 for register(getModEventBus())).

Shape: shapeless in effect (any arrangement), but exactly 3 items and exactly 1 of each - matches() rejects any stack with getCount() != 1 and any ingredientCount() != 3 (PathfinderQuillRecipe.java:46, :57-59). canCraftInDimensions is width*height >= 3 (:79-82), so the 2x2 inventory grid works, no crafting table needed.

All 15 are injected into the server's RecipeManager on every datapack reload (PathfinderQuillsModule.applyQuillRecipes, :79-94) as ids vanillaplusadditions:pathfinder_quill_<biome path>, CraftingBookCategory.MISC, via a LinkedHashMap merge + replaceRecipes - pure additions, nothing vanilla or Quark is overridden. No recipe JSON anywhere (house rule, CLAUDE.md).
notes:
SOURCE FILES (4, no resources at all): modules/pathfinder_quills/PathfinderQuillsModule.java, recipe/PathfinderQuillRecipe.java, recipe/PathfinderQuillRecipeSerializer.java, recipe/PathfinderQuillRecipes.java. No mixins (no mixin/pathfinder_quills/ package exists and vanillaplusadditions.mixins.json contains no entry matching quill/pathfinder), no lang keys (grep 'quill'/'pathfinder' over assets/vanillaplusadditions/lang/en_us.json: zero hits), no assets, no data JSONs, no TODO/FIXME, no command, no keybind, no client-only code (grep over the module for Minecraft.getInstance / net.minecraft.client / Dist.CLIENT / @OnlyIn / clientSetup / KeyMapping / RegisterCommandsEvent: zero hits).

CONFIG: constructor passes AbstractModuleConfig::createDefault (PathfinderQuillsModule.java:51) -> DefaultModuleConfig (AbstractModuleConfig.java:198-208), and buildModuleSpecificConfig is never overridden, so buildConfig (AbstractModuleConfig.java:50-74) adds ONLY the two universal keys 'enabled' and 'debug_logging' (AUTO). No module-specific config. enabledByDefault=true is the interface default (core/Module.java:73-75); only haunted_house overrides isEnabledByDefault anywhere in the codebase, this module does not.

CONFIG IS PER PHYSICAL SIDE: the spec is registered as ModConfig.Type.COMMON (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:131), so a client and a dedicated server each keep their own vanillaplusadditions-common.toml. Enabling the module on the server does not enable it on a connecting client - which matters here more than for most modules, see GOTCHA 1.

SIDE - why 'both' and not 'server': all behaviour is server-side (AddReloadListenerEvent, injection into the server's RecipeManager, crafting resolution). By the behaviour-only rule the sibling sheets use for custom_crafting_recipes and enhanced_ai_leader_loot this would be 'server'. The difference: those inject recipes that use VANILLA serializers, this one registers its OWN recipe serializer (vanillaplusadditions:pathfinder_quill) via DeferredRegister on the mod event bus (PathfinderQuillsModule.java:41-45, 62), and the 15 injected recipes are synced to clients encoded with exactly that serializer. PathfinderQuillRecipeSerializer's javadoc (lines 12-17) states the StreamCodec exists precisely to 'round-trip to the client (recipe book / JEI preview)'. A client without that registry entry cannot decode them. So the client-side half is load-bearing, not incidental -> 'both'.

GOTCHA 1 (the serializer registration is double-gated, and the gate is per side): RECIPE_SERIALIZERS.register(getModEventBus()) sits inside onInitialize() (line 62). AbstractModule.initialize (core/AbstractModule.java:90-105) returns at :96-99 unless shouldInitialize() is true, and ModuleManager only calls initialize() for config-enabled modules (core/ModuleManager.java:90-107). So the registry entry vanillaplusadditions:pathfinder_quill exists only where Quark is installed AND the module is enabled in that side's own COMMON config. A server that has both talking to a client that has Quark missing or the module switched off is the interesting case. Not reproducible from the repo - see 'unresolved'.

GOTCHA 2 (the javadoc's class-loading claim: substantially correct, with one nuance - this CORRECTS the first pass, which called it likely broken): PathfinderQuillsModule's javadoc (lines 31-37) claims shouldInitialize() keeps every Quark-referencing class from ever being classloaded without Quark. The static field QUILL_RECIPE_SERIALIZER (lines 41-45) IS initialized unconditionally when the class is loaded at `new PathfinderQuillsModule()` (VanillaPlusAdditions.java:188), but what it eagerly touches is Quark-free: DeferredRegister.create plus a constructor reference to PathfinderQuillRecipeSerializer, and that serializer class imports nothing from Quark (only com.mojang + net.minecraft). The single Quark-importing class is PathfinderQuillRecipe (import org.violetmoon.quark...PathfindersQuillItem, line 14), and it is reached only (a) when the serializer's supplier actually runs during the registry event - i.e. after the gated register(bus) - or (b) inside applyQuillRecipes, which only runs from the gated listener. PathfinderQuillsModule's own field types, signatures and gate method name no Quark type, which is exactly what the project memory 'Optional-Mod-Gates & Linking' (the beta.70 crash without Overpacked) demands. Residue without Quark: one unused DeferredRegister object. This is reasoning about JVM linkage, not a launch test - see 'unresolved'.

GOTCHA 3 (stricter than a vanilla shapeless recipe): PathfinderQuillRecipe.matches (lines 43-71) requires input.ingredientCount() == 3 (line 46) AND rejects the craft if any non-empty grid stack has getCount() != 1 (lines 57-59). Vanilla shapeless recipes ignore stack size, so a player who drops a stack of 3 Sand plus a Feather and an Eye into the grid gets no result and will conclude the recipe is broken. docs/modules/pathfinder_quills.md:7 calls it 'shapeless - any position in the grid' without mentioning the one-item-per-slot rule; the README paragraph (README.md:126-127) does not either. Order inside the grid genuinely does not matter (the else-if chain at :60-68 accepts the three items in any arrangement).

GOTCHA 4 (works in the 2x2 inventory grid): canCraftInDimensions returns width * height >= 3 (lines 79-82), so 2x2 = 4 qualifies and all 15 recipes are craftable without a crafting table. Neither README nor the module doc mentions it.

GOTCHA 5 (recipe-book unlock is unproven; JEI is fine): PathfinderQuillRecipe's javadoc (lines 16-22) and docs/modules/pathfinder_quills.md:50-51 claim the recipe 'shows up in the recipe book and JEI without any extra plugin'. JEI lists recipes regardless of unlock state and there is indeed no @JeiPlugin for this module (the five that exist are axolotl_guardian, battle_dogs, cat_guardian, free_anvil_repair, tipped_arrows), so the JEI half is plausible. The recipe-book half is not supported by anything in the repo: src/main/resources contains no advancement directory at all and no recipe-unlock data, and nothing in the module calls awardRecipes/recipeBook, so no player is ever granted the recipe. Vanilla recipe-book visibility depends on an unlock, which normally comes from a generated recipe advancement.

GOTCHA 6 (ingredient accessibility - honest in the doc, missing from the README): five biomes ask for that biome's own leaves (dark_forest, savanna, jungle, mangrove_swamp, cherry_grove), obtainable only with Shears/Silk Touch inside the biome you are trying to locate. docs/modules/pathfinder_quills.md:41-44 calls this a deliberate tradeoff; README.md:126-127 does not mention it.

GOTCHA 7 (the reverse-engineered table is VERIFIED - this CORRECTS the first pass, which left it unproven): libs/Quark-4.1-482.jar and libs/Zeta-1.1-40.jar are present locally, so the table was checked directly. javap -c on org.violetmoon.quark.content.tools.module.PathfinderMapsModule.register() yields exactly 15 loadTradeInfo(ResourceKey, Z, I, I, I, I) calls in this order with these color constants: SNOWY_PLAINS -8395521, WINDSWEPT_HILLS -7697782, DARK_FOREST -16754422, DESERT -3360434, SAVANNA -6576798, SWAMP -14534897, MANGROVE_SWAMP -14534897, OLD_GROWTH_PINE_TAIGA -10796513, FLOWER_FOREST -3258654, JUNGLE -14502400, BAMBOO_JUNGLE -12721641, BADLANDS -3768542, MUSHROOM_FIELDS -11713933, ICE_SPIKES -14761783, CHERRY_GROVE -1463832 - identical, in the same order, to PathfinderQuillRecipes.ENTRIES (lines 22-38). The duplicate -14534897 for swamp and mangrove_swamp is Quark's own value, not a typo here. Also verified: PathfindersQuillItem.forBiome(String, int) is public static and returns an ItemStack built from the static field PathfinderMapsModule.pathfinders_quill with the TARGET_BIOME / BIOME_COLOR / IS_UNDERGROUND=false data components, and PathfindersQuillItem extends org.violetmoon.zeta.item.ZetaItem - which is exactly why build.gradle needs Zeta on the compile classpath. Still true that a Quark update changing biomes or colors would silently desync crafted quills from traded ones, and nothing in the code detects that.

GOTCHA 8 (the gate checks the MOD, not Quark's own feature toggle): shouldInitialize only asks ModList.isLoaded('quark'). A pack that keeps Quark but switches Quark's own 'Pathfinder Maps' ZetaModule off in the Quark config still gets our 15 recipes. No crash results from that: javap on Zeta's ZetaModuleManager.constructAndSetup shows every discovered module is constructed and subscribed to the load bus with no enabled-check in front of it, so PathfinderMapsModule.register() runs and pathfinders_quill is assigned either way - forBiome cannot NPE on a null item. What a disabled Quark feature does to the quill's in-world search behaviour is Quark's business and was not tested.

GOTCHA 9 (recipe-map rewrite, cross-module coupling): applyQuillRecipes copies the entire current recipe map into a LinkedHashMap, adds the 15 entries and calls recipeManager.replaceRecipes(...) (lines 79-94). This is the house pattern, and it is used far more widely than the CLAUDE.md examples suggest: 13 module classes call replaceRecipes from an AddReloadListenerEvent listener (axolotl_guardian, battle_dogs, cat_guardian, compass_overhaul, custom_crafting_recipes, end_conduit, flying_fish, minecart_chunk_loading, mob_cart_loader, pathfinder_quills, stationary_chunk_loader, tipped_arrows, train_chunk_loading). Each listener re-reads the manager when it runs and preserves what it finds, so they stack; anything that replaced rather than merged would drop the quill recipes. Also: the listener is only attached while isModuleEnabled() (line 73), so switching the module off at runtime leaves the recipes live until the next /reload.

GOTCHA 10 (recipe ids use the biome PATH only): recipeId is 'pathfinder_quill_' + biomeId.getPath() (lines 87-89), so two target biomes with the same path in different namespaces would collide. All 15 entries are minecraft:, so this is inert today - it only matters if the table is ever extended with modded biomes.

BUILD: Quark AND Zeta must be on the compile classpath (build.gradle:152-160; PathfindersQuillItem extends ZetaItem, confirmed by javap, so javac must resolve the supertype even though our code never names Zeta). Both are compileOnly with deliberately NO localRuntime, so this module cannot be exercised in runClient/runServer - the build.gradle comment says to verify with the real deployed jar. All three CI workflows download both jars (build.yml:42-46, code-quality.yml:39-43 and :73-77, release.yml:39-43); CHANGELOG.md:328 records that code-quality.yml had to be taught this once the module landed in master. Zeta is not a runtime gate in our code (only 'quark' is checked), so it is not listed under requiredMods.

DEPENDENCY DECLARATION: neoforge.mods.toml declares create, toughasnails, sable, bluemap (all type='optional') and minecraft/neoforge - but NOT quark (grep count 0). So there is no declared load ordering relative to Quark; the runtime gate is the only link. This works because ModList.isLoaded is evaluated during module initialization and Quark's item field is filled by Quark's own registration.

STANDALONE JAR: pathfinder_quills is NOT in build.gradle's standaloneModules list (lines 386-465, alphabetically it would sit between 'options' and 'pet_potions' and does not) - bundle only, there is no vpa_pathfinder_quills jar.

REGISTRY ENTRIES: exactly one, the recipe serializer vanillaplusadditions:pathfinder_quill (PathfinderQuillsModule.java:41-45). No items, blocks or entities of its own - the crafted quill is Quark's item (quark:pathfinders_quill) built via PathfindersQuillItem.forBiome(biomeId, color) (PathfinderQuillRecipe.java:76 in assemble, :87 in getResultItem), the only Quark API this module calls.

HISTORY: the directory arrived in a single commit, c309098 (2026-08-29, 'Add tipped arrows from potions, netherite recipe rework, pathfinder quills, leader loot, egg stacking'); `git log --follow` over the module directory returns that one commit and nothing since. Earliest tag containing it: v1.0.0-beta.73.
